0.
0.1 This Indian

FOREWORD

Standard ( Part 3 ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 22 August 1983, after the draft finalized by the Power Line Carrier Systems and Associated Telecontrol Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Electronics and Telecommunication Division Council.

0.2 This standard ( Part 3 ) is intended to serve as a guide to installation engineers, contractors and users of power line carrier equipment, so far as coupling capacitors or capacitor voltage~transformers are concerned. 0.3 In view of the consideration that this code is required to be in conformity with the prevailing practices in this country, considerable assistance has been derived from the Indian Electricity Rules 1956 Reference to the relevant provisions of the while drafting this code. Indian Electricity Rules 1956 has therefore been made in appropriate places with a view to bringing to the notice of the installation and/or maintenance engineer(s) the statutory regulations concerning this work. 0.4 This standard ( Part 3 ) covers installation coupling capacitors/capacitor voltage transformers. this standard cover the following: Part 1 Line traps devices Part 2 Coupling and maintenance The other parts of of

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-196O*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.
*Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ).

1.1 This standard ( Part 3 ) coupling capacitors/capacitor used in outdoor installations.
2. TERMINOLOGY

covers installation and maintenance of voltage transformers ( CVT ) generally

the purpose of this standard, the definitions ( Part 4 )-1978* and IS : 9348-1979t shall apply.

given

in IS : 3156

3. EXCHANGE

OF INFORMATION

3.1 Before

ordering the coupling capacitor/CVT, information should be exchanged between the owner, switchyard designer, transmission line designer, installation engineer, maintenance engineer and manufacturer so that the coupling capacitor/CVT is procured to suit the duty, location and installation conditions under which it will operate.

3.2 The owner should obtain well in advance all relevant information about the overall dimensions, weight for transport, installation, etc, of the coupling capacitor/CVT. When the porcelain bushing, base tank and other accessories are separately packed, a packing list and drawings showing the assembly should be supplied to the user. 4. GENERAL

REQUIREMENTS

4.1 The

manufacturer should provide drawings and instructions for the installation and maintenance of the coupling capacitor well in advance of the time of delivery. It is essential that the installation of the coupling capacitor,`~CVT as well as its maintenance is performed in accordance with the instructions given by the manufacturer. 4.2 All electrical Indian Electricity installations shall comply with the requirements Act ( 1910 ) and Rules ( 1956 ) made thereunder. local of the

4.3 Applicable rules and regulations of the concerned if any, for the layout of installation should be observed. 4.4 The installation shall be carried out only competent to undertake such work under the rules may be in force in different states. 5. INSTALLATION

5.4 Clearances - All parts of the coupling capacitor/CVT are considered live and therefore minimum clearances between the coupling capacitor/CVT and other phases and between HV terminals of coupling capacitor/CVT and earth should be maintained in all conditions. Due allowances shall be given to take care of conductor movements and sagging in worst conditions. The recommended clearances are given in Table 1.

6. INSTALLATION
items of equipment should be carefully inspected as soon as possible upon arrival at site to ascertain whether they have been damaged in transit or whether any items are missing. Particular attention should be paid to the porcelain bushing. The base tank should be inspected for oil leakages. 6.2 Advice tendered by manufacturers for unpacking and lifting should be followed to prevent damage. Slingin g shall be carried out only at the lifting lugs provided for it. 6.3 In most cases, the base tank is supplied filled with oil. Tf the base tank is required to be filled, then the proper type of oil as recommended by the manufacturer and/or conforming to IS : 335-1972" shall be filled. ___-._
*Specification ravrsion) . for new insulating oils for transformers and switchgear ( second

6.1 All

G

IS t9859( Part 3 ) - 1983 Before filling with oil, the tank shall be thoroughly cleaned and material such as packing pieces, if existing, should be extraneous removed. The oil shall be thoroughly clean and dry before being filled The oil should be as warm as the surrounding air and into the tank. should be filled either with a centrifuging machine or filter press typ machine using flexible hoses. Rubber hoses shall not be used. 6.4 If the capacitor units and base tank are separately supplied, blanking plates are normally fitted on the tank cover and plugs are fitted to the breather pipe to avoid moisture absorption during despatch. During installation, the blanking plate should be removed. The capacitor units housed in porcelain bushings should be then fixed over the tank as per drawing. It should be ensured that there is good contact between the terminals of the capacitor units and between the terminal of the bottom most unit and terminal in the~base tank.
NOTE - The correct serial numbers of the capacitor units and base tank should be ascertained from test reports and assembled accordingly, since the final capacitance values are adjusted in the works for each combination of capacitor units.

The breather,

if any, should then be fitted into position.

6.5 The low voltage terminal ( carrier terminal ) should be connected to the drain coil by a single bare copper conductor or bare stiff copper strip. 6.6 The earthing terminals, normally provided on tank sides, should be connected to the switchyard earthing grid. 7. MAINTENANCE 7.1 For equipment with breather, the breather should be inspected at intervals of about 3 months, and if the blue silica gel crystals turn pink, these should be rea`ctivated by heating in an oven at 150�C until the crystals regain the blue colour. 7.2 Coupling capacitor/CVT should be disconnected from HV supply, at intervals of one year; capacitors should be discharged and the porcelain insulator inspected and cleaned. If the paint work on the tank is damaged, it should be repainted. The tank should be inspected for leaks.
